surface_forms: un vieux coureur de femmes comme lui

appraisal_events.evidence: "N'est-ce pas tout de même dégoûtant qu'un vieux coureur de femmes comme lui, qui n'a pas dételé, me donne perpétuellement des leçons et vienne m'espionner !"
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup privately accuses his uncle of hypocrisy, calling him an old womanizer who lectures and spies on him; this is filtered through Saint-Loup's whispered complaint rather than direct narrator endorsement.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Ne vous occupez pas de ce qu'il dit, il est un peu piqué... il dit cela parce qu'il croit que ça fait élégant, que ça fait grand seigneur d'avoir l'air jaloux"; she stamps her feet and hands in irritation, prompting Saint-Loup's own admission: "Tu nous rends ridicules aux yeux de ce monsieur."
appraisal_events.explanation: Rachel publicly dismisses and mocks Saint-Loup's behavior in front of the narrator, and her petulant display embarrasses him, a diminishment he himself acknowledges.

status_effects.explanation: Within the scene, Charlus is locally cast as a hypocritical, intrusive figure by Saint-Loup's whispered complaint, though this judgment is not independently confirmed by the narrator here.
Saint-Loup is publicly overridden and mocked by Rachel, losing composure and standing in front of the narrator and admitting the two of them look ridiculous.

ambiguities: Saint-Loup's condemnation of Charlus is presented as quoted private complaint (a whispered aside), so it is unclear whether the narrator endorses this characterization or is simply reporting Saint-Loup's perspective.
